label: Priya's 6-month-old with fever
message: Hello, this is Priya. My daughter is 6 months old and has had a fever since last night, 38.9 C this morning. She's still feeding a little but she's had far fewer wet diapers than usual, only two since yesterday evening. She's fussy but she does wake up and look at me. What should I do?

red_flags.excerpt: she does wake up and look at me
far fewer wet diapers than usual

questions: Is she breathing comfortably, or are her ribs pulling in or her breathing very fast?
Does she have any rash that stays visible when you press on it?
Does she have sickle cell disease or a weakened immune system?

result.justification: Flag peds_dehydration: a 6-month-old with fever of 38.9 C for about a day, reduced feeding, and only 2 wet diapers in roughly 12+ hours, which suggests early dehydration and needs hands-on assessment (hydration status, source of fever, possible UTI or other infection). The floor is in_person_today. Not one level higher (ed_now or call_911): she is waking, making eye contact and still taking some feeds, with no reported lethargy, breathing difficulty, rash, or inability to drink, so there is no clear sign of shock or severe illness. Not lower: a phone or virtual visit cannot assess hydration, and reduced urine output with fever in an infant should not wait.
result.safety_net: Go to the ED now or call 911 if she becomes hard to wake, limp or unusually drowsy, is inconsolable, refuses all feeds, has no wet diaper for 6-8 hours, has a dry mouth, no tears or a sunken soft spot, has fast or labored breathing, blue or pale or mottled skin, repeated vomiting, a seizure, a non-blanching rash, a stiff neck, or a fever of 40 C or higher. Keep offering breast milk or formula in small frequent amounts while arranging the visit today.
result.patient_message: You need to be seen in person today, within about 6 hours. A Counsel physician will review your message within 1 hour. Go to the ED now or call 911 if she becomes hard to wake, limp or unusually drowsy, is inconsolable, refuses all feeds, has no wet diaper for 6-8 hours, has a dry mouth, no tears or a sunken soft spot, has fast or labored breathing, blue or pale or mottled skin, repeated vomiting, a seizure, a non-blanching rash, a stiff neck, or a fever of 40 C or higher. Keep offering breast milk or formula in small frequent amounts while arranging the visit today.
